prompt:
Feature: show how many recipes use each tag and category, and merge one tag or category into another.

Group members who tidy their organizers cannot see how many recipes use a tag or a category. To fold a duplicate into another (say "Veggie" into "Vegetarian"), they have to re-tag every recipe by hand and then delete the old one.

Expected:

1. Recipe counts.
   - GET /api/organizers/tags and GET /api/organizers/categories add recipeCount (recipe_count) to every entry in items.
   - recipeCount is the number of recipes carrying that tag or category. It is 0 for an unused one, and 1 after a single recipe has been given it with PUT /api/recipes/{slug}.
   - The other fields stay as they are.
2. Merge endpoints: POST /api/organizers/tags/merge and POST /api/organizers/categories/merge.
   - The JSON body is {"fromId": "<uuid>", "toId": "<uuid>"} (fields from_id and to_id, with the usual camelCase aliases).
   - They need the same organizer permission as creating, updating or deleting organizers.
   - fromId equal to toId answers 400.
   - A fromId (or toId) that is not an organizer of the user's group answers 404, for example a random UUID.
   - Otherwise every recipe that carried the "from" organizer ends up carrying the "to" organizer instead.
   - A recipe that already carried both keeps a single link to "to". The merge must not hit the unique constraint on the recipe/organizer link table, and must not leave duplicates.
   - Then the "from" organizer is deleted, so GET /api/organizers/tags/{fromId} (or /categories/{fromId}) answers 404.
   - The changes are applied together: if anything fails, nothing is changed.
3. The merge response.
   - It answers 200 with the surviving organizer as JSON: its id (equal to toId), name, slug, groupId, and its recipeCount after the merge.
   - Example: "from" on one recipe and "to" on another gives recipeCount 2, and both recipes now list only "to".
   - Example: a single recipe carrying both gives recipeCount 1, and that recipe lists "to" but not "from".

Only tags and categories are in scope. The UI parts of the original change (showing the counts, a merge dialog, deleting unused organizers) are not part of this task.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/category_tag_tool_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: feat: organizer improvements — recipeCount, merge endpoint, delete unused UI (#7829)
